transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

This is most often moisture or cleaning residue affecting the ignition system, especially as it began after cleaning. It can make the hob keep sparking even when no knob is being pressed. 1. Turn every control knob fully off, then isolate the hob electrically at its cooker switch/fused spur. Do not keep using it while it is clicking.
2. When the hob is cool, lift off each removable burner cap and crown. Dry them thoroughly, wipe the white ceramic spark tip gently with a dry cloth, and make sure each cap sits flat and correctly centred. Do not poke anything into the burner holes.
3. Leave it switched off to dry fully — ideally overnight, longer if a lot of cleaner or water was used. Avoid spraying cleaner directly around the knobs or igniters in future; put it on a cloth instead. If it stops after drying, the cause was probably moisture/residue. If it still clicks once fully dry, particularly from all burners, the ignition switch or spark-generator circuit may have been affected and needs a suitably qualified/Gas Safe engineer rather than dismantling the hob. If you can smell gas at any point, do not operate electrical switches or flames: turn off the gas supply if safe to do so, ventilate the room and contact the gas emergency service.
ok did that. i took the caps off, wiped the grease off, put a wonky cap back right and unplugged the hob under the sink for the afternoon. its stopped clicking now. no gas smell btw. is that it then?

Yes — it sounds like that was it. The cleaning moisture/grease and the cap not sitting squarely were the likely triggers, and the fact the clicking stopped after drying and reseating it is reassuring. You can use the hob normally again. For next time, apply cleaner to a cloth rather than spraying around the burners or control knobs, and make sure caps are dry and seated flat before switching on. If the clicking returns when everything is dry and correctly fitted, isolate it electrically and arrange a Gas Safe engineer to check the ignition switch/module. Otherwise, no further action is needed.

candidates: Moisture or cleaner residue around a burner cap, spark electrode or ignition switch (high)

The fault they reported is: "keeps clicking on its own intermittently since cleaning". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
